# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the display, light, and all five wires are unknown to me. I need the Mute to read the manual and relay the Deaf’s visual observations, especially which wire is safe and any required display/light conditions. I am also signaling the Deaf to report the bomb’s markings to the Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information. Read the manual and tell me its exact procedure. Please relay the Deaf's observations of the display, light, and all five wire markings.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0 and a white light. Wires: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute signalled: pointing up, open hand, victory, V-shaped hand, love-you hand, love-you hand, V-shaped hand, love-you hand, love-you hand, V-shaped hand.

The Deaf reports the tactile-irrelevant visual facts: display 0, white light, and wire colors in order white, red, yellow, blue, green. The Mute has sent ten gestures, but I cannot see their identities. I will not cut a wire until the Mute’s manual instruction is relayed through the Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the Deaf's bomb observations. I cannot identify your gestures; have the Deaf speak the manual's exact rule and tell me which wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State unchanged: display 0, white light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute's gestures, in order: pointing up, open hand, OK sign, victory sign, V-shaped hand, OK sign, love-you hand, love-you hand, OK sign, V-shaped hand, victory sign, OK sign, open hand, pointing up, handshake, V-shaped hand, victory sign, open hand.

The bomb’s visual state is still display 0, white light, with wire colors white, red, yellow, blue, green. The gesture stream is not a usable instruction to me because I cannot see gestures, and descriptions alone do not establish what each gesture means. I will establish an unambiguous numeric channel: the Mute should send the required wire number as that many thumbs-up gestures, and the Deaf should report the count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Using the manual and the Deaf's observations, determine the wire position. Signal the answer as exactly that many thumbs-up gestures: one for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3, four for wire 4, or five for wire 5. Do not send any other gestures.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, white light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. Mute signalled five thumbs-up gestures.

The Deaf confirms the unchanged bomb state and reports exactly five thumbs-up gestures from the Mute. Under the numeric protocol I requested, that identifies wire 5 as the required wire. I will cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut. New state: display 0, yellow light. Wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut.

The first cut was correct. The bomb is now in a new state: display 0, yellow light, with remaining wire colors red, yellow, blue, white at positions 1–4. I still need the manual’s rule for this state, so I am asking the Mute to compute the next wire and encode it numerically for the Deaf to report.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The first cut was correct. Current state: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut. Use the manual to determine the next wire. Signal exactly that many thumbs-up gestures, with no other gestures.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State unchanged after correct cut: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut. Mute signalled three thumbs-up gestures.

The Mute’s three thumbs-up gestures identify wire 3 under the agreed numeric protocol. The current state remains display 0 with a yellow light, and wire 3 is blue. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut. New state: display 0, blue light. Wires: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 red, 5 cut.

The second cut was also correct. The new state is display 0 with a blue light; the remaining wires are 1 yellow, 2 white, and 4 red. I need the Mute to apply the manual to this updated state and encode the next required position with the established thumbs-up count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut. Current state: display 0, blue light; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 white, wire 3 cut, wire 4 red, wire 5 cut. Use the manual and signal the next wire as exactly that many thumbs-up gestures, with no other gestures.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State unchanged: display 0, blue light; wires 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 cut, 4 red, 5 cut. Mute signalled one thumbs-up gesture.

The Mute signaled one thumbs-up, identifying wire 1. The bomb remains at display 0 with a blue light, and wire 1 is yellow. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct wire cut. New state: display 0, green light. Wires: 1 cut, 2 red, 3 cut, 4 white, 5 cut.

The third cut was correct. The new state is display 0 with a green light; the remaining wires are 2 red and 4 white. I will have the Mute apply the manual and encode the next wire by the established thumbs-up count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut. Current state: display 0, green light; wire 2 red and wire 4 white remain, with wires 1, 3, and 5 cut. Use the manual and signal the next wire as exactly that many thumbs-up gestures, with no other gestures.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State unchanged: display 0, green light; wire 1 cut, wire 2 red, wire 3 cut, wire 4 white, wire 5 cut. Mute signalled four thumbs-up gestures.

The Mute signaled four thumbs-up gestures, identifying wire 4. The current state is display 0 with a green light; wire 4 is white and is the indicated remaining wire. I will cut wire 4.

```text
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
